content_html:
An air purifier with effective particle filtration can reduce fine dust that remains airborne, but it cannot prevent all dust from settling on furniture, fabrics, and floors. It works best alongside vacuuming, cleaning, and source control rather than replacing them.

It only filters particles that pass through the unit

A purifier has to move enough room air through its filter to make a meaningful difference. A small unit in a large room may capture particles near the device without substantially changing the overall room.

Coarse dust will still settle on surfaces

Fibers, hair, and larger particles often settle before reaching the purifier. Vacuuming with effective filtration, wiping surfaces, and reducing tracked-in soil are still necessary to see less deposited dust.

Choose capacity that matches the room

Compare the unit’s clean-air delivery or recommended room size with the actual space. Place it where intake and outlet airflow are not blocked by furniture or curtains.

Maintain the filter as the manufacturer specifies

A loaded filter reduces airflow and can increase noise. Replace or clean it on the specified schedule, and avoid devices that intentionally generate ozone in occupied living spaces.
